title_or_table: Small Area Health Insurance Estimates (SAHIE), counties, people under 65, all incomes, both sexes, all races
table_id: SAHIE timeseries, AGECAT=1, IPRCAT=0, SEXCAT=0, RACECAT=0, time=2024
geography: Counties and county equivalents in the 50 states and DC with an estimate, by Census region
unit: percent of people under 65 without health insurance; counties and outliers in counties. Quartiles by linear interpolation between ranked counties; whiskers at the last county inside 1.5 times the middle half
vintage: SAHIE 2024 release (the latest year in the data API on November 11, 2026)
qualification: Model-based estimates that combine survey and administrative data; small counties carry wide margins of error, so a box plot shows spread and no single county is ranked. Each county counts once, whatever its population, so the box describes counties, not people, and the note under the chart says so

counties.description: counties with an estimate, each counted once

whisker_low.description: lowest county rate at or above the lower fence

whisker_high.description: highest county rate at or below the upper fence

printed_source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Small Area Health Insurance Estimates, people under 65 without health insurance, 2024, counties in the 50 states and DC. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Model-based estimates; small counties carry wide margins of error; each region’s quartiles, whiskers and outliers computed by Oath & Action.
derivation: For each Census region, the counties with an estimate, each counted once: quartiles by Python's statistics.quantiles (method inclusive), fences at 1.5 times the middle half past each quartile, whiskers at the last county inside them, and a count of the counties past them (Tukey's box, the data lead's ruling (g))
notes: Counties with no estimate, left out: Kalawao County, HI
